<!-- pr-reviewer: bf7c0d068adaedd79a12721b0d618994447b4ed7 -->
Ready for the maintainer to merge.

## What looks good

- The post now reads the resolver flags (`g62Mode`, `g62TMaxUm`, #4226) and writes cycle 32 TOLERANCE for a section's smoothing ask (`PARAM Smoothing` / `SmoothingMode`, #616), replacing the old refuse. The Picomax path (no installed options) posts `32.0`/`32.1` only. Rough asks are refused by name there. The reset at the section end keeps no tolerance in the next operation.
- Refusals are named and use the same style as the DIN/ISO post: over-range T, T-rounds-to-0, no cycle 32 in profile, rough ask where HSC-MODE cannot be written, and the absence of a positive tolerance or a known mode. Duplicate declarations follow the existing baseline pattern (no conflict check for scalar params, as StartX/Coolant).
- A program with no smoothing ask is byte-identical: no existing golden changed; `unsupported_motion_or_missing_setup_data_is_refused` kept the same case count (one case changed from a finish ask to a rough ask, correctly refused on the Picomax).
- The new tests join the existing `script_goldens` suite via a `#[path]` include — no new test binary, and they sit in the `klartext/` suite directory. The new golden `picomax_smoothing.nc` is explained in the body; no snapshot PNG changed.
- The decision file `docs/decisions/4095-klartext-cycle-32.md` states the inference (the reset form `CYCL DEF 32.1` with no T) and the dropped options (a warning instead of a refusal, T-only with HSC-MODE on the Picomax, four-decimal T, no reset).
- Priority/effort honesty: the issue is P6/effort:max; the PR carries `Effort: max` and documents the inference. This is a post change, so the safety-floor awareness is recorded below. No dependencies, no process files, no `.github`, no `PROCESS_VERSION` edit, no snapshot PNGs. The body has a `Changelog:` line and ends `Refs #4095`; the title is conventional.

## Results merged with main

Built on the self-hosted runner (pr-test.yml, run https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/actions/runs/46077988043), merged with main `3c7cbe86056cdf306c7bfa6909bc7d5d94088542`, head `bf7c0d068adaedd79a12721b0d618994447b4ed7` ("The head is the one the reviewer read" passed). Quick gate: 35 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled, 28.2 min wall. No merge conflicts; the merge step passed. One site step skipped (environment: `zola`, `node` missing on the runner). Each relevant step was green:
- `post suites: script_goldens` (the new smoothing tests and `unsupported_motion_or_missing_setup_data_is_refused` included, 11 s), `post suites: script_dialects`, `post suites: script_arcs`, and the other post suites (lib, post_engine, cycles, edm, probe, rotary, wcs).
- `gcode suites: klartext` (546 s).
- `app suites: conformance`, `app suites: klartext_builtin`, and the shipped-example suites that the diff map runs: `example_catalog` (37 s), `example_catalog_adaptive` (1 s), `example_catalog_edge_work` (1 s), `first_part_programs`, `first_router_part`, `first_4axis_part`, `continuous_4axis_part`, `tilt_basis_compat`, `catalog_groove_part_off`.
- Clippy on the runner FAILED, but on the environment, not the code: `error: 'cargo-clippy' is not installed for the toolchain 'stable-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu'` — the runner's `cargo-clippy` is missing (`run rustup component add clippy`). The `camcraft-post` crate (the only crate touched) was re-run locally on the same head, merged with main: clean, no warnings (`cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`, 1m29s).
- Known residual: the local trial-merge used a slightly newer main (`b6089ea6e`, two MCP-only merges since the runner's fetch) — the post, machine files and tests the diff touches are unchanged by that delta; the runner's verdict and my local clippy/light lane both stand on the same code the PR touches.

## Targeted tests (step 5)

- Example catalog (this is a post change): the quick gate ran the catalog suites (`example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work` — green on the runner). No catalog case posts through the Klartext post (verified: no example catalog case names it), so no catalog-specific Klartext scenario is owed.
- Light lane `cargo xtask gate light` (this is the safety-floor lane for a post change): run locally on the trial-merged tree, 6 steps, 0 failed, 8.3 min wall (`motion light: lib` 399 s, `adaptive_troch_island` 55 s, `adaptive_troch_neck` 20 s, `adaptive_troch_parallel` 14 s, `app light: pocket_pass_start` 2 s). Green. This is the re-run the author promised in the quick pass ("I run the light lane again on bf7c0d0"); it was not posted before this review, and this review has it now.
- Heavy lanes: not run. Per the review law no PR gets the full heavy lanes. The PR is not a `P1` (it is a P6 enhancement), so the one targeted heavy step is not owed. The pinning tests, the post suites and the light lane above are the review's required coverage.

## Safety-floor awareness (this change posts G-code)

The change writes `CYCL DEF 32.0/32.1/32.2` blocks and the section-end reset. It is verified by: named refusals (never a silent wrong post), the golden, the pinning tests and the suite. **Not exercised:** a real iTNC 530 program — the reset form `CYCL DEF 32.1` with no T is inferred from the manual's NO ENT answer and is the same inference as the DIN/ISO post's bare `G62`. The machine builder must prepare the machine for cycle 32 (as for the DIN/ISO post). No real control, no human-verified output. Effort: max (safety floor); not escalated.

## Requested before merge

None.

## Questions / notes (not blocking)

1. The code refuses a tolerance with no mode when the control permits HSC-MODE (`tolerance without a finish or rough mode`), but the decision doc's refusal list does not mention this case. It is consistent with the DIN/ISO post (which refuses an undefined mode when P01 is written) and it refuses rather than mis-posts, so it is sound — but the doc and the code should agree. One line in `docs/decisions/4095-klartext-cycle-32.md` would close it.
2. `.toFixed(3)` rounds the tolerance before the µm check (0.0204 mm posts as T0.02, not refused). The DIN/ISO post uses the same 1 µm grid, so this is consistent; just note that the golden's 0.02 is grid-quantized.
3. The PR is merged green but the author's quick-pass note said the light lane would be re-run on this head; the note was never posted. This review ran it — see the targeted-tests section.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
